met_analysis:
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 74°E to the north of Lat. 32°N.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Uttarakhand and adjoining Himachal Pradesh at 0.9 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southeast Madhya Pradesh & adjoining Chhattisgarh at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Jharkhand & neighbourhood now lies over south Jharkhand & neighbourhood and extends upto 4.5 km above mean sea level.
The trough from Gulf of Mannar to Madhya Maharashtra now runs from Gulf of Mannar to North Interior Karnataka across Tamil Nadu and south Interior Karnataka at 0.9 km above mean sea level.
The trough from Sub-Himalayan West Bengalto Konkan & Goa now runs from Sub-Himalayan West Bengalto South Interior Karnatakaacross Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Vidarbha, Marathawada, North Interior Karnataka at 5.8 km above mean sea level.
The trough from west Uttar Pradesh to North Bay of Bengal now runs from southwest Uttar Pradesh to Northwest Bay of Bengal across northeast Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh & Odisha at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over South Haryana & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Coastal Andhra Pradesh & adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal at 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southeast Arabian Sea off south Kerala coast at 5.8 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
